Elaine (sales): Hey team — customer 'Northbridge' wants to run a 4-week POC. They need Hosted API keys + a Dedicated pool + VPC peering. Can we get a billing project with spend cap and initial credits?
Maria (billing): Sure. What spend cap and how many credits do they expect? Also need org_id and billing contact.
Elaine (sales): Asking for a $5k spend cap and $3k free credits to start. Org_id TBD (they'll provide this morning). Contact will be sophie@northbridge.com.
Rajesh (solutions): For Dedicated pool sizing, what throughput do they expect? If it's chat at 30 rps with batching, a single p4d-equivalent pool might be fine. Also confirm model family — we'll restrict to 7B/13B quantized to control cost.
Sophie (acct-mgr): Confirmed: 30 rps baseline, peak 60 rps. They want models similar to Llama2-13B and to avoid the 70B variants.
Chad (infra): VPC peering note: we need the customer's VPC CIDR, a peer subnet range, and a list of allowed egress IPs for firewall. Peering turnaround ~2 business days once we have those.
Maria (billing): To create the project I need: 1) customer_org_id 2) billing_email 3) spend_cap (USD) 4) initial_credits 5) allowed_models (comma list) 6) quota_limits (tokens/day, requests/min) 7) required_regions. Send those and I'll provision the billing project + invoice waiver for credits.
Elaine (sales): Got it. I'll collect: org_id, billing contact, CIDR, required regions (us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 backup), and allowed_models.
DevEx Bot: Pro tip: you can also provision a temporary project via CLI for testing: 
```
redwoodctl project create --org=<org_id> --name="northbridge-poc" --spend-cap=5000 --credits=3000 --models="llama2-13b-ql" --quota-tokens=500000 --quota-rpm=200
```
(returns project_id and ephemeral API keys). Ephemeral keys auto-expire after 14 days.
Rajesh (solutions): Also recommend setting routing policy to prefer dedicated pool and fallback to hosted small-models only. I'll add a canary policy so we don't auto-failover to 70B.
Chad (infra): For VPC peering we need a signed AUP from the customer (standard template), and their KMS key ARN if they want CMEK. If they want HSM, that's an extra security review.
Maria (billing): One caveat: credits are applied to project-level balance; spend cap blocks usage above the cap but isn't a hard block for Dedicated billing unless they accept invoice terms. We can enforce soft-block + alerts. Do they want hard stop?
Sophie (acct-mgr): Hard stop please — they can't exceed $5k during the POC.
Maria (billing): Hard stop requires signed contract addendum. Otherwise we can set alerts at 70/90% and automatic key rotation.
Elaine (sales): I'll attach addendum to the PO. Who needs to sign from infra/security?
Chad (infra): Security must sign the peering + KMS section. I'll loop in sec@redwood.internal.
Rajesh (solutions): To speed things up, here's the minimal payload Maria asked for — you can paste into the provisioning form or use the CLI: 
```
{
  "org_id": "<customer_org_id>",
  "billing_email": "sophie@northbridge.com",
  "spend_cap_usd": "5000",
  "initial_credits_usd": "3000",
  "allowed_models": "llama2-13b-ql",
  "quota_tokens_per_day": "500000",
  "quota_rpm": "200",
  "regions": "us-west-2,eu-west-1",
  "vpc_cidr": "<customer_cidr>",
  "kms_arn": "<optional_kms_arn>",
  "hard_stop_required": "true"
}
```
Maria (billing): Perfect — send that plus signed addendum and I'll provision the project and create the spendcap enforcement.
Elaine (sales): Thanks — I'll get everything today and post here. :thumbsup:
DevEx Bot: Note: once project is provisioned, generate ephemeral SDK keys for engs with `redwoodctl keys create --project <id> --type ephemeral --ttl 7d` to avoid exposing long-lived tokens.
Sophie (acct-mgr): One more ask from legal: can we restrict logs retention to 30 days for this POC?
Chad (infra): Yes, we can set retention per-project. I'll set default to 30d once we have project_id.
Elaine (sales): Great — will follow up this afternoon with org_id, signed addendum, CIDR. Thanks everyone!
DevEx Bot: Ticket #INC-7421 created to track provisioning steps and VPC peering.
